methods.label: Equidistant-point criterion
methods.explanation: A point equidistant from the endpoints of a segment lies on its perpendicular bisector. Both $C$ and $D$ satisfy this condition, so line $CD$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 8 perpendicular-bisector criterion and earlier facts about radii and lines.

methods.label: Congruent triangles at the midpoint
methods.explanation:
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). Equal compass radii give \(AC=BC\) and \(AD=BD\). Since \(AM=BM\) and \(CM\) is common, \(\triangle ACM\cong\triangle BCM\) by SSS. Their angles at \(M\) are therefore equal. These adjacent angles sum to \(180^\circ\), so each is \(90^\circ\), giving \(CM\perp AB\).

Applying the same argument to \(\triangle ADM\) and \(\triangle BDM\) gives \(DM\perp AB\). The perpendicular through \(M\) is unique, so \(C\), \(M\), and \(D\) lie on that line. Thus \(CD\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\), giving choice C.
methods.levelReason: Derives the construction using Grade 8 SSS and congruence properties with earlier midpoint and angle facts.
